answer: Proof of physical verification requires nodes to map a unique digital key to a ferrous hardware enclave, creating an oasis of identity trust amidst a sea of anonymous agents. By tying network participation to verified copper circuits, the system forces an attacker to acquire distinct, power-consuming physical units for every additional identity. This shifts the cost of a Sybil attack from negligible computation to significant capital expenditure, ensuring resource scarcity prevents mass identity forgery.
